headline: Anthropic reportedly flew a Hindu monk to San Francisco to discuss how its chatbot Claude should tell right from wrong, by the monk's own account.
score_reason: Unusual and widely covered in India, but it rests on one participant's account of a visit earlier in the year, unconfirmed by Anthropic.
importance_line: How an AI company decides what its chatbot should and should not do touches every user, and Anthropic appears to be asking religious and philosophical thinkers as well as engineers, though all of this is known only through the monk's own telling.
summary: The Economic Times reports that Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, flew Swami Sarvapriyananda of the Vedanta Society of New York to its San Francisco office earlier this year for closed sessions with theologians, counsellors and mental health professionals on AI ethics, according to the monk's own account that spread online this week; participants reportedly saw unreleased material and signed non-disclosure agreements. The paper stresses that Anthropic has not confirmed these details and has not claimed Claude is conscious, and places the visit alongside reported 'wisdom tradition circles' with thinkers from several faiths.
notes: Pool item was Firstpost (blocked, HTTP 403); read the same story on The Economic Times and credit it. The visit itself was 'earlier this year'; the news is the account surfacing on 2 to 3 Oct 2026.
